key_insight: CO-GRAFT shows that RL gains in search agents depend more on reasoning, search decisions, and answer extraction than query generation, which contributes at most 15% of the total gain.
engineering_relevance: Role-level attribution can help engineers target agent improvements rather than assume better search queries drive higher accuracy.
method: Combine RL-trained and pre-RL policies in one live-retrieval trajectory, assigning each of four functional roles to one policy.
Evaluate all 16 role assignments without changing weights or retraining.
Use Shapley values to allocate RL gains and Möbius terms to quantify role interactions.
evidence_signal: Evaluations span Search-R1 agents using Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2, two model sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, GRPO and PPO, and NQ and HotpotQA, with RL gains up to 32 exact-match points.
watch_item: Attributions depend on checkpoint characteristics and task-level search budgets; evaluating all 16 assignments also adds live-retrieval evaluation cost.
paper_title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
